Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General

Topic 5.2: Sign reading 5.2.1 Pre- sign reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign reading 5.2.1 Pre- sign reading, part of TIME Suggested vocabulary to be signed morning, afternoon, evening, night, day,  in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we learn letter sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign reading 5.2.1 Pre- sign reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Learner displays teamwork as they match target letters to their corresponding letter sounds.

• Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology as engage in letter matching activities using digital flash cards.

Values:
Unity: cooperation is nurtured as learner, in groups or pairs, play a fishing game by identifying specific letter sounds.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: effective communication is nurtured as learners develop confidence in their sign reading competency

Links to other Learning Areas:
Sign reading skills facilitate knowledge acquisition in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Manual alphabet chart, pocket charts, digital flash or flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate
